title: Staggered kernel sampling and soft-locks for KV fragment coordination
creator: Ariana Patel
description: Goal: Reduce prefill-triggered tail latency and unproductive KV fragment churn by coordinating kernel selection windows with a lightweight soft-lock reservation for KV segments. Background: Paged-attention workloads show bursts of short prefill waves that cause reactive evictions and repeated restores of small fragments. These create decode retries, kernel thrashing, and higher p99 token latency for interactive flows. This ticket designs and implements a two-part mechanism: 1) Staggered kernel sampling: the runtime will sample candidate kernels and their dwell windows for upcoming decodes and schedule prefill batches into non-overlapping kernel dwell slots where possible. Sampling leverages recent sequence length and KV-hit histograms per shard to bias kernel selection toward steady-state kernels for a short window. 2) Soft-lock fragment reservations: when a prefill decides to touch a fragment set, it will attempt a lightweight soft-lock that marks fragments as "reserved" for a configurable ttl (e.g., 80-200ms). Reserved fragments are exempt from speculative eviction and from expensive rehydration paths triggered by other concurrent decodes, reducing repeated readbacks. Implementation must be lock-free across CUDA streams and avoid interfering with multi-tenant fairness. Success criteria: - 20-35% reduction in prefill-triggered rehydrate ops on synthetic mixed short/long prompt workloads. - p99 token latency improvement >= 15ms for interactive small-batch decodes in our standard benchmark. - No measurable throughput regression (>2%) for heavy steady-state batching workloads. Out of scope: full tenant-level soft isolation; persistent reservation accounting across restarts. The ticket will deliver: design doc, runtime patches (kernel sampling scheduler, fragment soft-lock metadata path, eviction adapter), microbench harness, and experiment dashboard with before/after flamegraphs and KV rehydrate counts.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Bench harness reproduces fragmentation churn and measures rehydrate counts. 2) Staggered kernel sampling enabled via config flag; demonstration of scheduler placing prefill batches into non-overlapping kernel windows on 3-synthetic traces. 3) Soft-lock reserved fragments prevent speculative eviction during ttl and reduce duplicate rehydrates by >=20% on target traces. 4) No regressions in throughput or memory safety; CI stress runs pass N=3 10-minute soak tests. 5) Design doc and a PR with unit + integration tests reviewed and merged.
experiment_plan: 1) Add instrumentation counters for: kernel-dwell assignments, soft-lock reserve attempts/succeeds/fails, rehydrate counts, eviction decisions per fragment. 2) Run three trace profiles: conversational short-turn-heavy, mixed batch generation, and large-context long-prefill. 3) Sweep soft-lock ttl in [60ms, 120ms, 240ms] and kernel-window sizes [32ms, 64ms, 128ms]. 4) Compare baseline and patched runtime across p50/p95/p99 token latencies and rehydrate counts. 5) Surface results in a dashboard and attach flamegraphs for worst-case samples.
notes: Trade-offs discussed: soft-locks reduce eviction aggressiveness and may increase memory residency; mitigate with eviction score decay and soft-lock credit accounting per shard. Kernel sampling reduces kernel-switch overhead but may delay some prefill batches by a few ms; we will make sampling opportunistic and back off under high utilization. Need close coordination with autoscaler to avoid misinterpreting reservations as warm residency for scaling decisions.
comments: 2025-01-28 Ariana Patel: Created initial ticket. Observed repeated small-fragment rehydrates in Canary load tests causing p99 spikes. Proposal: coordinate kernel and fragment lifetimes rather than per-op greedy eviction.

2025-02-04 Liam O'Reilly: Spike implementation prototype complete for coarse-grained sampling and a proof-of-concept soft-lock metadata bit. Early microbench shows 18% rehydrate reduction on short-turn traces with ttl 100ms.

2025-02-12 Rahul Menon (reviewer): Reviewed approach. Concern: multi-tenant fairness when soft-locks accumulate; suggest per-tenant soft-lock budget and fail-open on budget exhaustion. Also requested metrics for 'soft-lock contention'.

2025-02-20 Engineering sync: Decided to implement per-shard soft-lock credits tracked in shard metadata; credits replenish on successful eviction and decay on inactivity. Sampling scheduler will expose a debug view in the Console to visualize dwell-slot occupancy.

2025-02-24 QA: Integration test added that simulates 50 concurrent small prefill requests and asserts no deadlocks on CUDA streams. Found a race where soft-lock release path could be delayed by GC; fixed by moving release to the decode completion callback.

2025-02-28 Performance: Full benchmark run on dedicated cluster (m6g/gpu equivalent). Results: mixed-batch p99 reduced by 12ms (baseline 96ms -> 84ms), rehydrate ops down 28% on conversational trace. Throughput unchanged within noise (+0.8%). Next: iterate ttl and sampling heuristics, prepare rollout config flag.

2025-03-01 Liam O'Reilly: Open PR #4892 contains implementation and tests. Requesting Canaries-on-Dedicated for runtime-1.22 if perf holds; will schedule smoke run and add Console dashboard panels for soft-lock metrics.
next_steps: 1) Land PR #4892 after addressing comments from Rahul (tenant soft-lock budgets). 2) Run two Canary shards in dedicated for 48h and monitor rehydrate and p99 token latencies. 3) Tune default ttl to 100ms and additive decay for credits. 4) Draft rollout doc for runtime-1.22 describing config flags and safety knobs.
